name: Microsoft (Entra ID / Graph)

verdict.headline: App registration takes minutes and publisher verification is free once your Partner Center (CPP) account is verified in 3–5 business days, but since Aug 2025 the default consent policy sends Mail, Calendar, Files and Chat scopes to each customer's admin even for verified apps, so plan for per-tenant admin consent.
verdict.nextAction: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and start Partner Center verification now, using a business email on the same domain you will set as the publisher domain.

appType: Multi-tenant Entra ID app registration (supported account type: Multiple Entra ID tenants), registered in a work or school tenant, not a personal Microsoft account

paths.name: Low-risk delegated scopes (User.Read, openid, profile)
paths.whenThisApplies: Your app only asks for basic sign-in and profile scopes. If the app is publisher verified and the customer tenant allows user consent, users can consent themselves and no admin approval is needed.

timeline.label: Verify your CPP account in Partner Center
timeline.note: Longer if Microsoft asks for more information.

timeline.label: Enter Partner ID and verify publisher
timeline.note: Microsoft states "a few minutes". Publisher verification itself is automated, with no separate provider review.

timeline.label: Appeal if verification is rejected
timeline.note: Only if Partner Center verification is rejected; no SLA for appeals.

paths.name: Admin-consent or blocked-by-default scopes (application permissions, Mail.*, Files.Read.All, etc.)
paths.whenThisApplies: Your app uses application permissions (always admin consent), or delegated scopes the Microsoft-managed default policy blocks from user consent: Files.Read/ReadWrite.All, Sites.Read/ReadWrite.All, Mail.*, Calendars.*, Chat.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Contacts/Tasks.*, People.Read, EWS/IMAP/POP/EAS.

timeline.label: Verify your CPP account in Partner Center
timeline.note: Longer if Microsoft asks for more information.

timeline.label: Enter Partner ID and verify publisher
timeline.note: Microsoft states "a few minutes". Publisher verification is automated.

timeline.label: Optional Microsoft 365 Certification audit
timeline.note: Optional yearly third-party audit with Claranet; no stated SLA. Publisher verification itself has no provider review.

timeline.label: Appeal if verification is rejected
timeline.note: Only if Partner Center verification is rejected; no SLA for appeals.

timeline.label: Admin consent in every customer tenant (the critical wait)
timeline.note: Needed in every tenant. Since Aug 2025 the Microsoft-managed default consent policy (microsoft-user-default-recommended) for new tenants blocks user consent to Files, Mail, Calendar, Chat and similar scopes even for verified apps, so each customer's admin must grant consent. How fast admins approve is unknown and outside your control.

beforeApproval.item: Users in other tenants see an "unverified" publisher on the consent screen and no blue verified badge.

Risk-based step-up consent is on by default: user consent goes to admin approval for newly registered multi-tenant apps that are not publisher verified and ask for more than basic sign-in and profile.
beforeApproval.detail: Users get AADSTS90094, or an "admin approval needed" request if the tenant has the admin consent workflow turned on.

beforeApproval.item: In your own tenant everything works, and any admin can consent.
No user caps or token quotas tied to verification were found.
Tenants using microsoft-user-default-low allow user consent only to apps from verified publishers or apps registered in that tenant.

prerequisites.item: An Entra work or school tenant
prerequisites.detail: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account (MSA) can't be verified. B2C and national clouds aren't supported.

prerequisites.item: A fully verified CPP Partner Global Account (PGA) Partner One ID
The app's tenant is linked to the PGA

prerequisites.detail: It must match the email domain used for CPP verification, or be a DNS-verified custom domain.
Entra: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator. Partner Center: CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin.

prerequisites.item: That person signs in with MFA and accepts the identity platform Terms of Use

prerequisites.detail: Checks your business email, identity (government ID), employment (domain registrar documents) and business registration documents.

steps.title: Create an Entra tenant
steps.detail: Create an Entra work or school tenant and give yourself at least the Application Developer role.

steps.title: Register the app as multi-tenant
steps.detail: App registrations → New registration, choosing Multiple Entra ID tenants.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can write the exact click path and field values to enter.

steps.title: Add redirect URIs and a credential
steps.detail: Add redirect URIs that follow Microsoft's rules (see gotchas) and a credential. Prefer a certificate or federated credential for production.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can draft the redirect URI list, check it against the redirect URI rules, and prepare manifest edits.

steps.title: Add Graph permissions
steps.detail: Delegated (scopes): users can consent to some, and admins can consent for everyone. Application (app roles): always need admin consent and must be requested with /.default.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can map your features to the minimal permission list, mark each delegated or application, and suggest narrower scopes such as Sites.Selected.

steps.title: Make the code multi-tenant
steps.detail: Point code at /organizations or /common, validate iss against tid, and cache tokens per tenant.

steps.title: Enroll in CPP and complete Partner Center verification
steps.detail: Submit business email, government ID, domain registrar documents and business registration documents.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can prepare a checklist of the documents and make sure the email domain matches your planned publisher domain.

steps.title: Microsoft verifies your Partner Center account
steps.detail: 3–5 business days, longer if Microsoft asks for more information.

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
steps.detail: In Branding & properties, set the publisher domain, choose Add Partner ID, then Verify and save. Takes a few minutes.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can run through the submission checklist with you before you click Verify.

steps.title: Test the verified badge
steps.detail: Sign in with prompt=consent to see the consent screen and badge. Use prompt=consent for testing only.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can build the test sign-in URL.

steps.title: Each customer's admin grants consent
steps.detail: The admin opens https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent?client_id=…&scope=…/.default&redirect_uri=…. Success returns admin_consent=True, and consent creates the app's service principal in their tenant.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can build the admin-consent link and a "connect" page for customer admins.

steps.title: Optional: Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation
steps.detail: A self-assessment. Most take an hour or less.
steps.agentHelp: An agent can draft answers from your security and data-handling practices for you to review.

steps.title: Optional: Microsoft 365 Certification
steps.detail: A yearly third-party audit with Claranet. Optional, though the docs say it "may be required" in some tenants.

submissionChecklist.item: Partner One ID is the PGA ID, and its status is Authorized
Tenant is linked to the PGA
Publisher domain is set, matches the CPP email domain, and is not onmicrosoft.com
Your account has both roles and signs in with MFA
submissionChecklist.detail: Entra Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator, plus CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin.

submissionChecklist.item: Permissions are minimal and listed correctly as delegated or application
There's an admin-consent link or "connect" page for customer admins

gotchas.title: Default consent policy blocks common scopes even for verified apps
gotchas.detail: "Let Microsoft manage your consent settings" (microsoft-user-default-recommended) is the default for new tenants, and Microsoft updates its list automatically. It blocks user consent to Files.Read/ReadWrite.All, Sites.Read/ReadWrite.All, Mail.*, Calendars.*, Chat.*, OnlineMeetings.*, Contacts/Tasks.*, People.Read, and EWS/IMAP/POP/EAS, even for verified apps. Consequence: customers' users can't self-onboard, and every tenant needs admin consent.

gotchas.title: The Aug 2025 rollout broke ISV onboarding
gotchas.detail: ISVs on Microsoft Q&A reported the policy change broke onboarding in Aug 2025 and say it was poorly announced. A secondary writeup tracks the expansion, with rollout by July 2026.

gotchas.title: Redirect URI rules
gotchas.detail: HTTPS only, except localhost. Case-sensitive, max 256 characters each. Max 256 per app for org-only apps, or 100 if you add personal accounts. No wildcards if personal accounts are enabled; for org-only apps they're possible through the manifest but discouraged. Query parameters are allowed only for org-only apps. Localhost ignores the port, and IPv6 [::1] isn't supported. http://127.0.0.1 can only be added by editing the manifest.

gotchas.title: Client secrets expire and are shown once
gotchas.detail: Max 24 months, and Microsoft recommends under 12. The value is shown only once. Microsoft recommends a certificate or federated credential for production.

gotchas.title: App ID URI must be globally unique
gotchas.detail: For multi-tenant apps the App ID URI must be globally unique, or the switch to multi-tenant fails. You can't move an app registration to another tenant.

gotchas.title: Admin consent without prompt=consent covers only the admin
gotchas.detail: If an admin signs in without prompt=consent, consent applies only to that admin's own account, not the whole tenant.

gotchas.title: Requiring user assignment forces admin consent
gotchas.detail: If a tenant requires user assignment for the app, admin consent is required.

blockers.whatToDo: Get publisher verified. Ask the customer to turn on the admin consent workflow, or send their admin the adminconsent URL.

blockers.symptom: Scope blocked by the Microsoft-managed consent policy
blockers.whatToDo: Plan for admin consent. Use a narrower scope, such as Sites.Selected or User.Read, where you can.

blockers.symptom: Partner Center verification rejected or stuck
blockers.whatToDo: Upload matching business and domain documents, then submit an appeal.

blockers.symptom: Publisher domain doesn't match the CPP email domain
blockers.whatToDo: Add a DNS-verified custom domain to the tenant.
